_comment: Itemization v2 (2026-08-27, designer's five-tier model). Every item has a 'tier' 1-5: T1 regular gear + Mastersmith weapons (+1 damage, mundane); T2 Enchanted +1 (weapons get 'hit': 1 and 'enchanted': true — ONLY enchanted weapons can strike monsters marked 'magic_to_hit' in monsters.json; armor +1 AC) plus minor trinkets; T3 enchanted with a minor ability/benefit/protection; T4 major; T5 unique named pieces. Vault chests draw gear from the floor's tier band (depth 1-4 -> T1 ... 17-20 -> T5). Supported magic fields on any worn piece: ac, sp, hit, dmg, detect, save_bonus, immune (condition ids), abilities ({str:+1}), enchanted. Weapons: 'finesse' aims with best of STR/DEX, 'hands': 2 claims both hands, 'range' makes it a bow. Potions: effect heal/cure/mana (dice) or invisibility (battle-only: the drinker fades until they strike). ALL stats here are Claude PROPOSALS under the designer's model — retune freely. | TIER ABILITIES (2026-08-27 session 2): 'resist': [elements] = HALF damage from that element (designer ruling — damage only); 'immune' also takes elements (zero damage AND blocks the linked condition: fire->burning, poison->poison); weapon 'bonus_damage': {dice, element} adds a named elemental die per hit; weapon 'double_vs': family + 'flavor' word doubles the FINAL damage total vs that monster family (Ancient=undead/holy, Bane=outsider). Elements: fire/frost/lightning/poison (electricity = lightning). | PRINCIPLE (designer, 2026-08-28): WEAPONS carry offensive minor abilities, ARMOR/clothing defensive ones — the T3 elemental blades add flat +1 elemental damage (bonus_damage dice may be a flat number); resist/immune belong on worn pieces. | MAGIC v3 (2026-08-28): scrolls. A spell with 'scroll': true in spells.json becomes the item 'scroll_<spell>' automatically; explicit scroll entries here (type 'scroll' + 'spell') override that. 'scroll_values' = the price ladder by spell level, x 'rare_multiplier' for rare lore; tier defaults to the spell level. Any arcane caster reads a scroll once in battle; only a spellbook copies it.
